cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and what deserves your attention is already plain.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: When something hard sits between you and someone, say it quietly and say it once, then stop there rather than saying it again in softer words.
cells.core:
Something in you knows what deserves attention before it can explain why. In a loud conversation you are already leaning toward the part that counts, and the people near you feel the lean. Then the pull to move them toward what you have recognized starts working before the recognizing has finished. A truth from a second ago gets said as a plan, or as a story with a lesson tucked inside, and the person is being moved before they've arrived.
When a hard thing sits between you and someone, say it gently and only once. Don't circle it, don't repeat it, don't quietly turn it into a principle. Put it down where it belongs and stop. If you've misjudged how it will land, you've lost nothing but the second telling, and the second telling wasn't doing the work anyway.
cells.sheetLine: What matters is clear to you. Say it once.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a meaning you intend to make arrive.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Ease forward by one small step whatever you've been trying to change between yourself and another person all at once, no announcement and no checking whether it worked.
cells.core:
You can feel where a conversation is heading before it starts, and when it matters, you start steering before the other person has spoken. The charge toward connection outruns the moment. What should be a living exchange becomes an outcome that gets secured, so the people in it hear the need in your voice. Nothing gets to rest as it is for an hour.
Ease the situation that matters between you and someone else forward by a single inch. Slowly. No plan laid out, no follow-up meeting. Structures that needed to fall will fall on their own; the ones you force usually won't. You find out which this is by moving the inch rather than the room, and what happens after belongs as much to the other person as to you.
cells.sheetLine: You aim the meaning before the person has arrived.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that shut behind you, still facing it.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: State the logic of something you keep circling without deciding, in a single clean sentence, then do that sentence — just the plain cut, no wide feeling required.
cells.core:
You have been near conversations about what matters without moving them. The charge toward connection is still there, but these days it stays abstract — you can name what counts and not put it in front of anybody. What you know has gone thin, kept for yourself, and the ones who used to get the live version get only the summary. What you haven't done isn't a mystery, and it isn't a wound. It simply hasn't been done.
Don't try to feel your way back in. Reason it through, fast and clean, and the sharp point arrives through the reasoning rather than ahead of it. Whatever the cut costs you is smaller than another year of the summary version — and the summary version is not what anyone is waiting for.
cells.sheetLine: You know what matters and haven't put it in front of anyone.

cells.tense: Your hand is still while a room is being moved by a voice that sounds like you.
cells.act: hold the clarity steady and tempered
cells.ask: Keep the clear thing even and steady at whatever moment finds you holding a room's attention, and don't hand what you did away to circumstance or mood.
cells.core:
People leave your conversations steadier than they came, and if you described afterwards what happened, you'd say you mostly listened. But the steadying came from you — your phrasing, your pace, your choice of what to leave unsaid. You hold rooms with a level sentence and then file it as something said rather than something you did. The account has nobody in it, and the account itself is where the work begins.
At whatever moment finds you holding the room's attention, keep the clear thing steady and even, and don't give the credit away — not to circumstance, not to the other person, not to the mood. If it feels exposed, that exposure is the part worth keeping. What you do for people holds up better when you can stand inside it as the one doing it.
cells.sheetLine: You steady whole rooms and file it as listening.
